body:
**Stable key:** `MEM-P05`  
**Difficulty:** **High**  
**Suggested label:** `difficulty:high` (metadata proposal; a title/body marker does not depend on label availability)  
**Planning baseline:** `Ozwasyd/FsusBlog@580cf1af614fd0edab9cb4c9ee95ec4e128b0327`  
**Acceptance predecessors:** `MEM-P01` (#3445), `MEM-P04` (#3448)

### Objective

Provide the portable unmanaged host backend without changing the language, public protocol, or physical-residency guarantees of the operating system.

### Source and scope precedence

This issue implements stage P05 of the user-supplied memory-governance report (version 1.0, 2026-09-15). The user's later requirement for default automatic discovery and activation supersedes `Preferred`, default-off, and mandatory manual-per-capability opt-in wording. Original work-item IDs are preserved for traceability. Baseline paths must be checked against the actual implementation candidate; this issue is not a claim that proposed types already exist.

### Mandatory policy and terminology

All configurable capabilities default to `Auto` when omitted. `Auto` means automatic discovery, bounded qualification, online activation, and deterministic selection for an eligible workload after resource admission. It does not mean indiscriminate allocation. A supported, release-qualified and runtime-qualified available path must not require a second enable flag, per-host approval file, or administrator confirmation. `Disabled` prevents new capability-specific probes and use, and drains existing owners before disposal. `Required` adds a strict requirement; it does not override safety, permissions, qualification, or budgets. The earlier report value `Preferred` is superseded, not an additional mode.

Detection, qualification, online state, effective path, and per-operation admission are separate facts. Unknown, Unsupported, NotVerified, Faulted, Disabled, and temporarily BudgetRejected are not synonyms. A missing signal is not zero usage. Qualifying a release/backend is not a manual opt-in on each deployment. The always-required accounting, ownership, and content-security rules are not optional capability switches.

### Scope and exclusions

No direct system VM API, GPU allocation, published Realloc, whole-process custom GC, or immediate-RSS-reclaim guarantee is included.

All product implementation introduced by this memory program remains C#/.NET. Supported already-installed OS/GPU APIs may be called through isolated C# adapters. Existing unrelated C++, frontend, protocol, and business components are not rewritten. Do not change AEDS/HTTP, authorization, revocation, publication, or delivery authority merely to simplify memory management.

### Files and ownership

| Status | Path or owner | Required treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Host/` | Segmented arena, builders, block owners, and MemoryManager implementation. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Lifetime/` | Block-held lease and pin integration. |
| N | `src/backend/Infrastructure/Memory/Accounting/` | Capacity charging and ownership transfer adapters. |
| R | `Existing backend project unsafe boundaries and test project` | Register unsafe scope and tests with the current owners. |

B = baseline-reported; N = proposed-new; R = exact owner unresolved until MEM-P00. Paths and namespaces in this table are scope locators, not permission to create a parallel registry, publisher, scheduler, configuration source, or test runner. New tests must reside inside the actual owning project.

### Required implementation work

- [ ] **P05.1** Use bounded blocks rather than one mandatory allocation for an entire generation. Calibrate normal block sizes from P01, define a separately bounded oversized-blob class, restrict each CPU view to the supported length range, and use checked arena-wide accounting.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC01`, `MEM-P05-AC02`, `MEM-P05-AC10`.
- [ ] **P05.2** Confine NativeMemory calls to the backend. Pair Alloc with Free and AlignedAlloc with AlignedFree. Validate capacity, alignment, arithmetic, allocation failure, and disposed state. Published blocks must not be reallocated or moved in place.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC01`, `MEM-P05-AC02`, `MEM-P05-AC08`.
- [ ] **P05.3** Implement a block owner and MemoryManager that retain the raw address, capacity, state, lease/pin counts, and ledger charge. Pin/Unpin must participate in release safety without claiming OS page locking or GPU registration.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC05`, `MEM-P05-AC07`.
- [ ] **P05.4** Use one builder owner or explicitly partitioned writes. Expose only fully initialized logical slices. Seal transfers ownership, closes the writable API, and prevents new writable leases; failure before transfer cleans all builder-owned resources.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC03`, `MEM-P05-AC04`, `MEM-P05-AC06`.
- [ ] **P05.5** Report allocator relinquishment separately from observed OS reclamation. Do not label BCL allocation capacity as exact OS committed/resident bytes. GC.AddMemoryPressure must not be used as the budget mechanism or charged with disk/VRAM bytes.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC10`.
- [ ] **P05.6** Provide allocation-failure, boundary-canary, reuse, duplicate-disposal, stale-write-view, length-limit, and partial-build-cleanup tests. Isolate deliberate access-fault tests from the test runner.

  Acceptance mapping: `MEM-P05-AC02`, `MEM-P05-AC03`, `MEM-P05-AC04`, `MEM-P05-AC05`, `MEM-P05-AC08`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC01** All native allocations obtain a reservation before the allocator call; actual block capacity, including rounding, is charged. The allocation/free event stream has correct allocator pairing and no unmatched live allocation after drain.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC02** Invalid alignment and checked size/offset overflow are rejected before memory access. Requests exceeding a CPU view limit cannot wrap into a smaller allocation.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC03** For every published slice, only its initialized logical range can be read, hashed, serialized, or sent. A canary-filled unwritten tail never appears in externally consumed bytes.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC04** Seal transfers exactly one ownership responsibility. A disposed builder does not free a successfully transferred block; a failed Seal leaves no unowned block or reservation.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC05** An active reader or pin prevents release even when all snapshot roles have ended. Duplicate disposal does not free twice or make a still-live old handle refer to a reused block.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC06** Capturing a writable view does not create a false claim of physical write protection. The public builder API grants no new writes after Seal, escape points are audited, and actual OS read-only protection remains a separate capability.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC07** Native and managed backends pass the same lease and byte-output contracts. NativeMemory mode requires no GPU, custom native product module, NUMA API, or special privilege.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC08** After native allocation failure N, previous sealed data remains readable and unchanged, partial new work is cleaned, and accounting returns to its precisely expected state.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC09** Host backend discovery advertises native availability and qualification inputs for MEM-AUTO. The standalone backend does not introduce a hidden manual enable flag or select itself on a request path.
- [ ] **MEM-P05-AC10** Capacity, logical usage, fragmentation, retained bytes, and observed RSS are distinct fields. A failure of RSS to fall immediately is not mislabeled as either proven leakage or proven reclamation.

### Required validation scope

Real native allocator/lifetime integration and target-platform baseline tests; transport barriers may use the dedicated native-consumer harness before PublicHotRead integration.

| Scenario | Responsibility in this issue | Required observable assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `T05`: Invalid, extreme, aligned, multiplied, or offset sizes | Primary implementation owner | Reject invalid or overflowing arithmetic before allocation and memory access; never wrap a large request into a small allocation. |
| `T06`: Allocator fails on allocation N | Primary implementation owner | Clean only the candidate-owned resources; earlier sealed data remains valid and outstanding accounting is correct. |
| `T07`: Several generations or variants share one block | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P03 | Charge the allocation once and explain separate role/reader references; retain it until all actual holds end. |
| `T08`: Pool rent, return, retention, and trim | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P14 | Lease return is distinct from retained ownership and OS reclamation; retained capacity stays charged. |
| `T10`: Transport write remains incomplete while the snapshot retires | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | No release before actual consumer completion; eventual release after all remaining holds end. |
| `T13`: Repeated disposal, ownership misuse, and outstanding pins | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P04 | Release is idempotent or rejected explicitly; no underflow, double free, or stale-token/ABA reuse. |
| `T16`: Unwritten tail or padding in a candidate buffer | Primary implementation owner | Uninitialized data cannot enter a response, integrity calculation, published record, or disk format. |
| `T17`: Attempt to write after Seal | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P16 | Grant no new writable view; an OS-protected backend actually prevents the write in an isolated process. |
| `T50`: Portable targets across declared OS and x64/ARM64 combinations | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P19 | Run the same contracts on each claimed target; no hidden layout, visibility, or loader assumptions. |
| `T56`: Repeated build, retirement, compaction, migration, and recovery | Required local assertion/fixture contribution; primary owner MEM-P19 | No unexplained persistent ownership growth; explain retained capacity using actual events. |

### Evidence and acceptance rules

Every unchecked acceptance criterion below is mandatory. `must` and `must not` are normative; `may` grants an option only where it is explicitly stated. A required test passes only when its specified assertion is observed on the current candidate. A comment stating that an assertion is true is not evidence.

Bind evidence to the actual commit and worktree fingerprint, fixture, toolchain, configuration revision, backend, OS/architecture, relevant driver/device identity, actual command, and raw result. Use the existing test DAG, required static admission, fixture ownership, and independent verifiers. All numeric limits and performance expressions referenced by this issue must be finite, explicit, and frozen by their owning policy/baseline before candidate results are examined. Missing values block acceptance; do not invent a passing threshold afterward.

Expected resource rejection must not conceal use-after-free, bounds violations, double free, uninitialized disclosure, revoked/wrong content, negative accounting, a parallel authority, or an unbounded queue. Any such correctness failure blocks acceptance regardless of performance. Do not rewrite frozen receipts or weaken tests. Missing platform or hardware evidence is `NotVerified`, not `Passed` or a convenient `NotApplicable`.

Evidence level is stage-specific: contract or fixture work may run before a downstream backend exists, but it does not certify that backend. Each primary implementation owner must supply its own required integration/platform evidence; MEM-P19 independently closes the complete matrix. Passing tests never authorizes automatic closure of this issue, another issue, or a pull request.

### Safe disable and rollback

Stop creating new native generations, select the qualified managed backend for subsequent work, and drain existing native owners. Do not copy the entire cache back into RAM.

### Completion report

Report the exact scope and files changed, every acceptance-criterion result, tests and commands actually run, raw current-source evidence, default Auto behavior, negative/competition cases, performance against frozen gates where applicable, unresolved support rows, and rollback results. A missing required environment leaves the corresponding promise unverified. Do not describe planned tests or a passing document validator as product verification.

Docker-related tests are not to be executed by this delivery agent under the project restriction. State them explicitly as not run. A Docker-specific assertion requires evidence from its authorized owner; a genuinely technology-independent assertion may use authorized non-Docker isolation. Do not fetch missing implementation dependencies from the network; record exact package/version/target gaps and stop the blocked execution item.
